---
title: "Package and portfolio action plan"
---

The deliverable is a reusable Python package and a Quarto portfolio website built from the same executable notebooks. The user journey is **initialize one match → browse team possessions → choose any usable frame → compute quantities → retrieve and plot → summarize a possession**. Documentation describes this journey before introducing equations and internal solvers.

## 1. Define the data and object contract — implemented

Keep `PRESS(tracking_data, ...)` as the main entry point. Construction validates inputs and establishes per-frame result stores; it does not execute costly solvers. Optional explicit team/player interval and action tables enable navigation. `PRESS.from_skillcorner` loads the already processed match files and standardizes action context for checkpoint use. Separate team-possession IDs, player segments and frame IDs throughout the API.

The team reconstruction only links verified successful receptions. No possession boundaries are invented from tracking carrier changes alone. Inspect excluded checkpoint rows before a report and retain source action IDs for audit. [Data contract and errors](api.qmd).

## 2. Make the common analysis path explicit — implemented

Provide getters for team intervals, player intervals, tracking frames, states and eligible checkpoints. Provide `compute_frame` for arbitrary-frame evaluation and `compute_possession` for trajectories on a chosen sampling. The accepted default uses canonical action starts plus separately marked short-tail/terminal evaluation snapshots; `include_snapshots=False` keeps canonical rows and explicit `frame_ids` supports another sampling. This default is inspired by action-based EPV organization [@fernandez2019] and will be reviewed in the benchmarks. **design choice** Resolve event context independently through frame annotations or containing action intervals, with explicit overrides. Retain the component compute methods for research and inspection. Clear dependent results after a component is recomputed. Keep BCOS in `PRESS.extras`; its scalar feature is supplied explicitly at the low-level selection API or calculated by the orchestration method.

The [run guide](usage.qmd), [workflow vignette](vignettes/00_match_workflow/00_match_workflow.ipynb), and `examples/checkpoint.py` show the complete flow on synthetic data and explain how to swap in local match files.

## 3. Give each task an executable vignette — implemented

| Task | Vignette and API |
|---|---|
| Initialize and inspect a match | 00 · match workflow; constructor, possession/frame/checkpoint getters |
| Carry loss | 01 · ball-drive risk; `compute_ball_drive_loss`, drive getter |
| Pass execution | 02 · pass probability; `compute_ppcf`, PPCF getter |
| Destination choice | 03 · transition model; `compute_transition_probabilities`; features and sources |
| Pass-versus-carry choice | 04 · action selection; `compute_action_selection_probability`; features and BCOS link |
| Conditional terminal continuation | 05a · residual risk; fifth main component vignette and optional xLoss completion |
| Mixture risk and labels | 05 · hazard and bands; `compute_frame`, hazard getter, `hazard_to_band` |
| Team units and checkpoint selection | 06 · possession setup; interval/frame/checkpoint getters |
| Possession difficulty | 07 · survival; `compute_possession`, `possession_survival` |
| Pressure patterns | 08 · three report patterns, eligibility denominators and close-engagement case; historical eight-label helper distinguished |
| Cohort summaries and case studies | 09 · league report; category aggregation and deterministic case selection |
| Optional open-space field | Extra BCOS; separate class, getter and plot |
| Event-derived location value | Extra xT; Bellman iteration, citation, shape/orientation and grid lookup |

Each notebook includes the task, inputs, model assumptions, a code-generated visual, a runnable package example and interpretation/limits. Synthetic inputs are labelled and enable execution without redistributing match data. Coarse demo grids are distinguished from the model’s default research settings. References distinguish published ideas from project choices.

The fifth main component, [residual risk](vignettes/05a_residual_risk/05a_residual_risk.ipynb) documents the completed RR77 conditional terminal benchmark and `PRESS.extras.compose_individual_xloss`; it remains outside the core pressure pipeline. The [composed-risk benchmark](vignettes/05b_composed_risk_benchmark/05b_composed_risk_benchmark.ipynb) separately evaluates h and individual xLoss.

## 4. Build documentation and portfolio together — implemented configuration

Use `api.qmd` for the public contracts, `solvers.qmd` for low-level scientific signatures, `usage.qmd` for the main workflow, and the notebooks as both downloadable executable source and website pages. `_quarto.yml` supplies navigation, citations and rendering. Keep notebook outputs and generated figures reproducible with `scripts/rebuild_vignettes.py`; use `scripts/check_docs.py` to check source links, references and examples. Dependency pins match the verified Python environment; `scripts/check_environment.py` checks them. After rendering, `scripts/check_site.py` verifies local HTML links, assets and anchors. Generated bytecode and build metadata are excluded from Git.

GitHub Actions verifies the package, examples and website on pull requests and pushes to `development`/`main`; publication occurs only on `main`. GitHub Pages needs its repository setting switched to GitHub Actions. Local HTML review requires the pinned Quarto CLI. Configuration is not evidence that a deployment already happened.

## 5. Validation and research work after this packaging change

Before reporting performance, define eligible possession/checkpoint coverage across all ten matches, inspect conservative team-link breaks, and choose the case-study policy. Rebuild component predictions on shared match-level folds to evaluate the final composed hazard without in-sample component leakage. Populate the benchmark page with actual results and reproducible code; leave the existing placeholder until this analysis is complete.

A first public release should follow review of the API, rendered pages, data attribution, learned-model provenance and the benchmark’s actual scope. Publishing and release tagging are separate actions. This packaging change does not claim new validation results.

For pipeline migration targets, script responsibilities and existing file contracts, see the [pipeline layout](pipeline.qmd).

## Repository responsibilities

| Location | Responsibility |
|---|---|
| `PRESS/core/press.py` | Match object, navigation, compute orchestration, component result stores |
| `PRESS/utils/match.py` | Provider adapter, interval validation and event-category mapping |
| `PRESS/utils/possession.py` | Bands, retrospective survival and typology rules |
| `PRESS/datasets.py` | Fresh deterministic synthetic inputs for examples |
| `PRESS/model/`, `PRESS/physics/` | Existing numerical solvers and physics primitives |
| `PRESS/extras/` | Optional models such as BCOS |
| `examples/`, `tests/` | Runnable user entry points and behavioral API checks |
| `vignettes/`, `*.qmd`, `_quarto.yml` | Executable explanations, function reference and portfolio site |
| `scripts/`, `.github/workflows/` | Rebuild, source checks, continuous verification and main-branch publication |

## Migration map

| Earlier access / location | Current package structure |
|---|---|
| BCOS methods in the main class | `PRESS.extras.BCOS`; core action selection receives the scalar feature |
| `vignettes/10_bcos/10_bcos.ipynb` | `vignettes/extras/bcos/10_bcos.ipynb` |
| Manual tracking filters and direct result-store reads | Public possession/frame/checkpoint getters and component result getters |
| Manually ordered compute calls | Retained component APIs, plus `compute_frame` and `compute_possession` wrappers |
| Separate prose and toy figures | Executable notebooks with both an explanatory visual and a package-usage example |
| Existing `PRESS/` package and physics modules | Retained paths; no forced migration to `src/press/` |
| Machine-specific raw-data preprocessing/training scripts | Remain in the sibling analysis repository; processed-file adapter and table contracts are provided here |

```text
PRESS/
  core/press.py
  datasets.py
  extras/bcos.py
  model/  physics/  visualization/
  utils/match.py  utils/possession.py  utils/data/
examples/checkpoint.py
tests/test_match_workflow.py
vignettes/00_match_workflow/ ... 09_league_level_report/
vignettes/extras/bcos/  extras/expected_threat/
usage.qmd  api.qmd  solvers.qmd  roadmap.qmd
_quarto.yml  index.qmd  data.qmd  benchmark.qmd
scripts/rebuild_vignettes.py  scripts/check_environment.py
scripts/check_docs.py  scripts/check_site.py
.github/workflows/verify.yml  .github/workflows/publish-site.yml
```


The BCOS extra now contains the conceptual definition, conditional-hazard mathematics, a real tracking-frame calculation and a Brisbane–Perth spatial/temporal case study, with aggregation support and numerical checks. The h/bands vignette now contains the decision-level definition, exact band thresholds, checkpoint conventions, three context-checked matching-fold trajectories and all fifteen canonical pitch snapshots. The composed h/xLoss benchmark has a separate page. The linked pattern and team/player report vignettes now contain real frozen OOF summaries, contextualized cases, explicit opportunity denominators and uncertainty. These are ten-match sample profiles, not full-season rankings. The primary score is terminal retention per distinct pressure-exposed individual possession; action-level observed–expected remains secondary. Residual-risk example and benchmark are complete; the verified 118-tree deployment refit78 is installed.
